old: It's named not for what it looks like, but for who once oversaw a French colony.
The flower's genus name honors a 17th-century French governor.
Botanists borrowed the surname Bégon, honoring Michel Bégon, to name this plant.
clues: This flowering plant, a favorite in gardens and on windowsills, was named as a tribute to a 17th-century French governor of the Caribbean colony Saint-Domingue.
Shade gardeners prize its fleshy stems, lopsided patterned leaves and waxy pink, red or white blooms; unlike impatiens, many kinds are grown more for foliage than flowers.
Look for the rex kind with painted leaves or the tuberous kind with rose-like blooms; botanists coined its name to honor Michel Bégon.
